newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - United Waste on EPS view.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - United Waste on EPS view.

text.p: United Waste Systems Inc chairman and chief executive Bradley Jacobs said Tuesday he was "generally comfortable" with analysts's earnings estimates ranging from $1.45-$1.50 per share for the 1997 year.
In an interview with Reuters, Jacobs said he was also "not uncomfortable" with 1996 estimates of about $1.06 per share. The company earned $0.78 per share in 1995.
He said the company planned to make acquisitions this year of companies with annualized revenues of $150-$200 million, with such deals a key part of its future growth strategy.
In 1996, United Waste completed 79 acquisitions with about $152 million in annualized revenues, Jacobs said.
The waste disposal company said it will grow both internally and via acquisitions.

As for acquisitions, United Waste's strategy has been to primarily buy smaller, privately-held companies, operating within its existing service areas, like California and the Rocky Mountain region, Jacobs said.
Earlier Tuesday, the Greenwich, Conn.-based company announced it recently completed 20 acquisitions with annualized revenues of about $43 million.

The purchases consisted of four landfills, 27 waste collection companies and eight transfer stations. About $19 million of the acquired revenues were in northern California and $17 million were in the Rocky Mountain region, it said.
"We continue to evaluate acquisition opportunities in California," Jacobs said. "The Rocky Mountain area, like Colorado, New Mexico and Arizona, also has big potential."
He said United Waste has also identified a number of interesting opportunities in the Northeast, and in such states as Kentucky and West Virginia.
